title: Dune
author: Frank Herbert
description: On the desert planet Arrakis, young Paul Atreides is caught between noble houses, a spice monopoly and a prophecy. A dense political epic about power, religion and ecology.

title: Neuromancer
author: William Gibson
description: Case is a burned-out console cowboy hired for one last job by an artificial intelligence. The founding cyberpunk novel: neon, decks, and corporate decay.

title: The Left Hand of Darkness
author: Ursula K. Le Guin
description: An envoy visits an ice-bound world whose inhabitants have no fixed gender, and must learn to understand a culture before he can negotiate with it. Quiet, political, deeply humane.

title: The Hobbit
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
description: A comfortable hobbit is dragooned into a quest for dragon gold. The gentlest possible introduction to epic fantasy.

title: Piranesi
author: Susanna Clarke
description: A man lives alone in an infinite house of statues and tides, keeping careful notes. A strange, tender puzzle about memory and kindness.

title: The Name of the Wind
author: Patrick Rothfuss
description: A legendary magician tells his own story: a childhood in a troupe, years in a brutal university, and a talent for naming things.

title: Gone Girl
author: Gillian Flynn
description: A woman vanishes on her fifth wedding anniversary and her husband becomes the story. A cold, clever thriller about performance and public opinion.

title: The Big Sleep
author: Raymond Chandler
description: Private eye Philip Marlowe takes a blackmail case for a dying general and finds the family rotten underneath. The template for hard-boiled detective fiction.

title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
description: Holmes and Watson investigate a family curse on the foggy Devon moors. Atmospheric, methodical Victorian detection.

title: Educating Rita
author: Willy Russell
description: A hairdresser enrols in an Open University literature course and refuses to be condescended to. A two-hander about class, appetite and change.

title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
author: Yuval Noah Harari
description: A sweeping account of how Homo sapiens came to dominate the planet through shared fictions: money, nations, religions and corporations.

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
description: The two-system model of mind: fast intuition and slow reasoning, and the predictable ways each one misleads us.

title: The Design of Everyday Things
author: Don Norman
description: Why doors confuse us and interfaces frustrate us, and how good design makes the right action obvious. The classic text on affordances.

title: Project Hail Mary
author: Andy Weir
description: A lone astronaut wakes with no memory aboard a ship sent to save a dying sun, and solves one engineering problem at a time. Warm, funny, relentlessly competent.

title: The Martian
author: Andy Weir
description: An astronaut is stranded on Mars and has to science his way to survival. Told largely through logs, with a very high tolerance for duct tape.

title: A Canticle for Leibowitz
author: Walter M. Miller Jr.
description: After nuclear war, monks preserve the scraps of scientific knowledge as holy relics. A long, wry meditation on history repeating itself.

title: Beloved
author: Toni Morrison
description: A formerly enslaved woman is haunted, literally, by her past. Demanding and extraordinary.

title: Never Let Me Go
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
description: Three friends at an English boarding school slowly understand what they are for. Devastating precisely because of its restraint.

title: The Remains of the Day
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
description: An English butler takes a motoring holiday and reviews a life spent in service, and the feelings he never permitted himself.

title: The City and the City
author: China Mieville
description: A murder investigation in a city that shares its streets with another invisible city, and the elaborate rules that keep them apart.
